title: Run three cooperating containers
instructions:
Run all commands and create all local files for this exam on the initial controller, using its supplied kubeconfig. All questions use this single cluster; no context switching is required.

In namespace `container-lab`, create Pod `trio-runner` with exactly three containers:
- `alpha`: image `busybox:1.28`, environment variable `ORDER=LEAD`.
- `web`: image `nginx:1.27`, declare container port `8081`.
- `omega`: image `busybox:1.31.1`, environment variable `ORDER=TAIL`.

All three must remain running. Supply a long-running command to the BusyBox containers. The declared nginx container port is metadata; this task does not require changing nginx's default listener.
steps: Write a v1 Pod manifest with three containers.
Set each image, name, environment value, and the web containerPort.
Use sleep commands to keep BusyBox running, apply the manifest, and wait for Ready.
solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: trio-runner
  namespace: container-lab
spec:
  containers:
  - name: alpha
    image: busybox:1.28
    command: [sh, -c, 'sleep 7200']
    env: [{name: ORDER, value: LEAD}]
  - name: web
    image: nginx:1.27
    ports: [{containerPort: 8081}]
  - name: omega
    image: busybox:1.31.1
    command: [sh, -c, 'sleep 7200']
    env: [{name: ORDER, value: TAIL}]
YAML

checks.description: Three correctly configured containers are running

explanation: Containers share a Pod network namespace. Declaring containerPort does not reconfigure the application listener.

title: Define a static-storage class
instructions: Create StorageClass `cedar-static` with provisioner `kubernetes.io/no-provisioner`, volume binding mode `WaitForFirstConsumer`, and volume expansion enabled. Only the class definition is required; the expansion flag does not itself make static volumes expandable.
steps: Create a storage.k8s.io/v1 StorageClass manifest.
Set provisioner, volumeBindingMode, and allowVolumeExpansion as requested.
solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata: {name: cedar-static}
provisioner: kubernetes.io/no-provisioner
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
allowVolumeExpansion: true
YAML

checks.description: StorageClass matches all fields

explanation: WaitForFirstConsumer defers binding until the scheduler has placement information.

title: Schedule a process report
instructions: In `batch-lab`, create CronJob `process-report` using image `node:22-bookworm`. Every 20 minutes it must execute `ps -eaf` through a shell to list all running processes. Do not suspend the CronJob.
steps: Use cron schedule */20 * * * *.
Set the container command to sh -c 'ps -eaf' and restartPolicy to OnFailure or Never.
solution: kubectl -n batch-lab create cronjob process-report --image=node:22-bookworm --schedule='*/20 * * * *' -- sh -c 'ps -eaf'

checks.description: CronJob runs the process command in a shell every 20 minutes

explanation: CronJobs create Jobs on a schedule; the shell must be explicit when required.

title: Keep an Ubuntu container running
instructions: In `pod-workshop`, create Pod `ubuntu-rest` with container name `ubuntu-agent`, image `ubuntu:24.04`, and a command that sleeps for 7200 seconds. The Pod must be running.
steps: Write a Pod manifest with the required container name and image.
Set command to sleep 7200 and create the Pod.
solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: ubuntu-rest, namespace: pod-workshop}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: ubuntu-agent
    image: ubuntu:24.04
    command: [sleep, '7200']
YAML

checks.description: Ubuntu Pod has the requested command and is running

explanation: A Pod needs a continuing foreground process to remain running.

title: Split traffic between application versions
instructions:
In `default`, deploy 10 application Pods across two Deployments, sharing Service traffic approximately 60% / 40%:
- `azure-web`: 6 replicas, image `kodekloud/webapp-color:v1`, Deployment label and Pod label `track-one=azure`.
- `jade-web`: 4 replicas, image `kodekloud/webapp-color:v2`, Deployment label and Pod label `track-two=jade`.
- Both Pod templates must also carry `release=stable`.

Create NodePort Service `release-entry`, port `8081`, target port `8080`, selecting `release=stable`. Keep both Deployments healthy. The ratio is based on ready endpoint counts, not an exact per-request guarantee. Test with curl against any node's DHCP IP and the allocated nodePort; node addresses are available with `kubectl get nodes -o wide`.
steps: Create the two labeled Deployments with six and four replicas.
Give both Pod templates the shared release=stable label.
Create a NodePort Service selecting that shared label and forwarding 8081 to 8080.
solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: azure-web, labels: {track-one: azure}}
spec:
  replicas: 6
  selector: {matchLabels: {track-one: azure}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {track-one: azure, release: stable}}
    spec:
      containers: [{name: web, image: 'kodekloud/webapp-color:v1', ports: [{containerPort: 8080}]}]
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: jade-web, labels: {track-two: jade}}
spec:
  replicas: 4
  selector: {matchLabels: {track-two: jade}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {track-two: jade, release: stable}}
    spec:
      containers: [{name: web, image: 'kodekloud/webapp-color:v2', ports: [{containerPort: 8080}]}]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: release-entry}
spec:
  type: NodePort
  selector: {release: stable}
  ports: [{port: 8081, targetPort: 8080}]
YAML

checks.description: Both versions are ready with the requested split and working NodePort

explanation: A common Service selector distributes connections across the selected ready endpoints.

title: Repair a crashing application
instructions: Deployment `bulletin-web` in namespace `dev-workshop` has crashing containers. Inspect events, logs, and its configuration, fix the cause, and leave its existing nginx application serving HTTP on port 80 with 2 ready replicas. Do not replace the application with a sleep process or remove its readiness probe.
steps: Inspect Pods and logs in dev-workshop.
The nginx startup command references an invalid configuration path; remove that override.
Wait for two ready replicas and check HTTP service.
solution:
kubectl -n dev-workshop patch deployment bulletin-web --type=json -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/command"}]'
kubectl -n dev-workshop rollout status deployment/bulletin-web --timeout=180s

checks.description: Existing application is healthy and serves HTTP

explanation: Logs and container command overrides can reveal startup configuration mistakes.

title: Repair and install a Helm chart
instructions:
A broken Helm chart is provided on the initial controller at `/opt/lantern-chart`. Fix the templates and update `values.yaml` and `Chart.yaml`, then install it with release name `lantern-web` in namespace `frontend-workshop`.

Required values: `replicaCount: 4`, `service.type: NodePort`, and chart `appVersion: "1.21.0"`. Keep image `kodekloud/webapp-color:v1`; appVersion is chart metadata, not an image tag. The chart creates Deployment and Service named after the release. All four application Pods must be ready and the Service must reach them.
steps: Inspect the selectors in both templates and align them with the Pod labels.
Set values.yaml replicaCount to 4 and service.type to NodePort; set Chart.yaml appVersion to 1.21.0.
Run helm upgrade --install lantern-web /opt/lantern-chart -n frontend-workshop --create-namespace --wait.
solution:
sed -i 's/app: broken-selector/app: {{ .Release.Name }}/g' /opt/lantern-chart/templates/*.yaml
sed -i 's/replicaCount: 1/replicaCount: 4/; s/type: ClusterIP/type: NodePort/' /opt/lantern-chart/values.yaml
sed -i 's/appVersion: "1.0.0"/appVersion: "1.21.0"/' /opt/lantern-chart/Chart.yaml
helm upgrade --install lantern-web /opt/lantern-chart -n frontend-workshop --create-namespace --wait --timeout 180s

checks.description: Chart files, Helm release, replicas, and working Service match

explanation: Deployment selectors must match template labels, and the Service must select those same Pods.

title: Expose an existing Pod
instructions: Pod `parcel-web` already runs in `default` and listens on port 80. Using an imperative command, create ClusterIP Service `parcel-entry` exposing it within the cluster on port `6445`, targeting port `80`.
steps: Inspect the Pod labels.
Use kubectl expose pod with port 6445, target-port 80, and the required Service name.
solution: kubectl expose pod parcel-web --name=parcel-entry --port=6445 --target-port=80

checks.description: ClusterIP Service selects the Pod and serves HTTP on 6445

explanation: Service port and application targetPort may differ. Final-state grading cannot prove an imperative command was used.

title: Isolate a namespace
instructions: Create namespace `sealed-workshop`, which does not yet exist. In it, create NetworkPolicy `isolate-everything` selecting all Pods and denying all ingress and egress. Do not add allow rules or other policies in this namespace. The cluster enforces Kubernetes NetworkPolicies.
steps: Create the namespace.
Use an empty podSelector and both Ingress and Egress policyTypes.
Set ingress and egress to empty lists.
solution:
kubectl create namespace sealed-workshop
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: isolate-everything, namespace: sealed-workshop}
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
  ingress: []
  egress: []
YAML

checks.description: Namespace has a deny-all ingress and egress policy without competing allowances

explanation: NetworkPolicy allowances are additive; both traffic directions must be explicitly isolated.

title: Repair access to an external web server
instructions:
An HTTP server runs directly on the initial controller host, outside Kubernetes, on port `9998`. All nodes can reach the controller's DHCP/InternalIP address; discover it with `kubectl get nodes -o wide` (the node labeled `node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane`).

In `default`, selectorless Service `host-web-entry` should expose that server to Pods on port `8082`, but its endpoint address and port are wrong. Repair its existing `host-web-backend` EndpointSlice so Pods can retrieve the server response `ckad001-host-web` through `http://host-web-entry:8082`. Preserve the selectorless Service.
steps: Discover the controller InternalIP.
Inspect host-web-entry and its EndpointSlice.
Correct the IPv4 endpoint and its port to the host address and 9998, then test from a Pod.
solution:
ip=$(kubectl get nodes -l node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.addresses[?(@.type=="InternalIP")].address}')
kubectl patch endpointslice host-web-backend --type=merge -p "{\"endpoints\":[{\"addresses\":[\"$ip\"],\"conditions\":{\"ready\":true}}],\"ports\":[{\"name\":\"http\",\"protocol\":\"TCP\",\"port\":9998}]}"

checks.description: Selectorless Service points at the real host server and is reachable from a Pod

explanation: A selectorless Service can route to an external backend via a manually managed EndpointSlice.

title: Publish an application inside the cluster
instructions: In `default`, create Pod `message-web` using `kodekloud/webapp-color:v1` with label `tier=messages`. Create ClusterIP Service `message-entry` selecting that label, exposing port `6381` and forwarding to the application's port `8080`. Ensure the Pod is ready and the Service works.
steps: Create and label the application Pod.
Create a ClusterIP Service with selector tier=messages and ports 6381 to 8080.
solution:
kubectl run message-web --image=kodekloud/webapp-color:v1 --labels=tier=messages
kubectl expose pod message-web --name=message-entry --port=6381 --target-port=8080

checks.description: Pod, labels, and working ClusterIP Service match

explanation: Services discover Pods by labels, not their resource names.

title: Create an external DNS alias
instructions: In `default`, create ExternalName Service `resolver-alias`, declaring UDP port `53` and externalName `dns.google`. This is a DNS alias task: ExternalName requires a DNS hostname for useful resolution and does not proxy traffic to an IP literal.
steps: Create a v1 Service with type ExternalName.
Set externalName to dns.google and declare UDP port 53.
solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: resolver-alias}
spec:
  type: ExternalName
  externalName: dns.google
  ports: [{port: 53, protocol: UDP}]
YAML

checks.description: ExternalName and DNS port match

explanation: ExternalName returns a DNS CNAME; it does not create ordinary Service proxy endpoints.

title: Configure and report Burstable QoS
instructions:
In `qos-workshop`, create Pod `elastic-web`, image `nginx:1.27`, container name `elastic-container`, with resource settings giving it QoS class `Burstable`.

Retrieve every Pod's name and QoS class in this namespace, including its existing Pods, and save the output on the initial controller as `/root/qos-report.txt`. Use two whitespace-separated columns headed `NAME QOS`, followed by one row per Pod. Use sudo to write under /root if needed.
steps: Set a CPU request without an equal matching limit, then create the Pod.
Wait until Kubernetes assigns its QoS class.
Use custom-columns to collect names and status.qosClass and save the report with sudo tee.
solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: elastic-web, namespace: qos-workshop}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: elastic-container
    image: nginx:1.27
    resources: {requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 32Mi}, limits: {memory: 96Mi}}
YAML
kubectl -n qos-workshop wait pod/elastic-web --for=condition=Ready --timeout=180s
kubectl -n qos-workshop get pods -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,QOS:.status.qosClass | sudo -n tee /root/qos-report.txt >/dev/null

checks.description: Burstable Pod and complete, accurate QoS report exist

explanation: Burstable Pods have some resource requests or limits but do not meet the Guaranteed criteria.

title: Create a custom resource from its schema
instructions: Discover the installed CRD whose name contains `anime`. In `default`, create resource `evening-series` of kind `Anime`, specifying title `Cowboy Bebop` and episode count `26`. Inspect the CRD schema to identify its API version and spec fields.
steps: Use kubectl get crd and inspect the anime CRD.
Create an Anime using spec.title and spec.episodes.

checks.description: Custom resource matches the discovered schema and requested data

explanation: The CRD establishes the resource's API group, scope, and validation schema; an operator is not required for this task.

title: Build a ConfigMap from environment files
instructions: Create ConfigMap `workshop-settings` in `default` using all key/value pairs from both `/root/workshop-env/app.env` and `/root/workshop-env/cache.env` on the initial controller. Store the environment entries as individual ConfigMap keys, not as whole files. You may use sudo to read the files.
steps: Inspect both supplied environment files.
Use repeated --from-env-file flags with kubectl create configmap.
solution: kubectl create configmap workshop-settings --from-env-file=<(sudo -n cat /root/workshop-env/app.env) --from-env-file=<(sudo -n cat /root/workshop-env/cache.env)

checks.description: ConfigMap contains every supplied environment entry

explanation: Repeated --from-env-file arguments merge entries into individual ConfigMap keys.

title: Load database settings from a Secret
instructions:
Namespace `database-workshop` contains Pod `ledger-client` and its supporting database Service. Create Secret `ledger-settings` with exactly these keys and values: `DB_Host=sql02`, `DB_User=ledger`, `DB_Password=practice456`.

Reconfigure the existing Pod to import all keys from this Secret as environment variable names using envFrom.secretRef. Preserve its image and application command; recreate the Pod if necessary. It must run successfully with the imported settings.
steps: Create the Secret with three literal entries.
Export the Pod, remove generated metadata/status, and add envFrom.secretRef.
Delete and recreate the Pod, preserving its existing application.
solution:
kubectl -n database-workshop create secret generic ledger-settings --from-literal=DB_Host=sql02 --from-literal=DB_User=ledger --from-literal=DB_Password=practice456
kubectl -n database-workshop get pod ledger-client -o json | jq 'del(.metadata.uid,.metadata.resourceVersion,.metadata.creationTimestamp,.metadata.managedFields,.status) | .spec.containers[0].envFrom=[{"secretRef":{"name":"ledger-settings"}}]' > /tmp/ckad001-ledger.json
kubectl -n database-workshop delete pod ledger-client --wait=true
kubectl create -f /tmp/ckad001-ledger.json

checks.description: Secret values and live imported application environment match

explanation: envFrom imports Secret keys without individually mapping each variable.

title: Limit ResourceQuota objects
instructions: Create namespace `quota-workshop` if needed. Create ResourceQuota `quota-object-cap` in that namespace enforcing a maximum of one ResourceQuota object. Either `resourcequotas: "1"` or `count/resourcequotas: "1"` is accepted.
steps: Create the namespace.
Create a ResourceQuota with hard count/resourcequotas set to 1.
solution:
kubectl create namespace quota-workshop
kubectl -n quota-workshop create quota quota-object-cap --hard=count/resourcequotas=1

checks.description: ResourceQuota limits its own resource kind to one object

explanation: Object-count quotas can limit resource kinds, including ResourceQuota itself.

title: Mount a Secret read-only
instructions:
Use the supplied Pod template `/root/workshop-secret-pod.yaml` on the initial controller to create Pod `vault-reader` in `secret-workshop`. Preserve its container name, image, and command.

Add volume `credential-volume` backed by existing Secret `vault-settings`. Mount it in the container at `/etc/credentials` with `readOnly: true`, so the existing `.token` Secret key is accessible there. Use sudo to read or edit the template.
steps: Copy the template to a writable location.
Add a Secret volume and its read-only volumeMount.
Create the Pod and inspect the mounted .token file.
solution:
sudo -n cat /root/workshop-secret-pod.yaml > /tmp/ckad001-vault.yaml
cat >> /tmp/ckad001-vault.yaml <<'YAML'
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: credential-volume, mountPath: /etc/credentials, readOnly: true}
  volumes:
  - name: credential-volume
    secret: {secretName: vault-settings}
YAML
kubectl create -f /tmp/ckad001-vault.yaml

checks.description: Template Pod mounts and reads the Secret at the required read-only path

explanation: Secret volumes support dotfile keys and should be mounted read-only.

title: Add an HTTP readiness probe
instructions: Existing Pod `warmup-web` in `default` uses image `kodekloud/webapp-delayed-start`. Recreate it, preserving its image, with an HTTP readinessProbe: path `/ready`, port `8080`, initialDelaySeconds `20`. Wait until it becomes Ready. Adding a probe requires recreating the Pod.
steps: Export the existing Pod and remove generated metadata and status.
Add the HTTP readiness probe, delete the original Pod, and recreate it.
Wait for application startup and a successful readiness probe.
solution:
kubectl get pod warmup-web -o json | jq 'del(.metadata.uid,.metadata.resourceVersion,.metadata.creationTimestamp,.metadata.managedFields,.status) | .spec.containers[0].readinessProbe={"httpGet":{"path":"/ready","port":8080},"initialDelaySeconds":20}' > /tmp/ckad001-ready.json
kubectl delete pod warmup-web --wait=true
kubectl create -f /tmp/ckad001-ready.json

checks.description: Application has the requested HTTP readiness probe and is ready

explanation: Readiness determines whether a Pod is eligible for Service traffic.

title: Repair a Pod manifest
instructions: The initial controller has a broken manifest at `/root/workshop-busybox.yaml`. Correct the file and create its Pod `toolbox-rest` in `default`. Preserve container name `toolbox`, image `busybox:1.36`, and its long-running command. Ensure it uses the correct Pod apiVersion and is running. Use sudo to edit the file.
steps: Inspect the manifest and correct the Pod apiVersion to v1.
Apply the corrected file and wait for Ready.
solution:
sudo -n sed -i 's/apiVersion: apps\/v1/apiVersion: v1/' /root/workshop-busybox.yaml
sudo -n cat /root/workshop-busybox.yaml | kubectl apply -f -

checks.description: Source manifest is corrected and matching BusyBox Pod is running

explanation: Pods are core/v1 resources, not apps/v1 resources.

title: Configure an exec liveness probe
instructions: In `default`, create Pod `redis-watch` using image `redis:7.4`. Add a livenessProbe executing command `ls` with initialDelaySeconds `8`. Keep the Pod running. You may generate the initial manifest imperatively with kubectl run --dry-run=client.
steps: Generate a redis Pod manifest.
Add livenessProbe.exec.command [ls] and initialDelaySeconds 8.
Create the Pod and verify it is ready.
solution: kubectl run redis-watch --image=redis:7.4 --dry-run=client -o json | jq '.spec.containers[0].livenessProbe={"exec":{"command":["ls"]},"initialDelaySeconds":8}' | kubectl create -f -

checks.description: Redis is running with the requested exec liveness probe

explanation: An exec probe succeeds when its command exits with status zero.
